lines.text: Ever touched a door handle and got ZAPPED? Here's why.
When Dash shuffles across the carpet, his rubber soles rub the fibers and steal tiny particles called electrons.
Rubber won't let them escape, so they spread all over him. Even his hair stands up: the extra electrons push each other away.
By the door, he's carrying about ten thousand volts.
Metal is an easy road for electrons, so they rush into his fingertip,
and jump the last few millimeters all at once. A tiny bolt of lightning!
Lots of volts, but far too little current to hurt. Just a sting.
Newt's trick? Touch the metal with a key first. The spark hits the key, not your skin.
